clouds-beginner.title: Painting Clouds — Beginner
clouds-beginner.blurb: Start from nothing. Twelve lessons that take you from an empty page to a cloud that reads as a solid, sunlit object — the drawing underneath, the three values that make it fluffy, and the four cloud families you will paint for the rest of your life.
learn: Set up a small, honest kit and a desk that does not fight you
Draw the geometry underneath a cloud before any water touches paper
Sort any sky into light, grey and dark — the whole trick behind “fluffy”
Paint cumulus, stratus and cirrus, then mix them in one sky
who: Complete beginners
No drawing experience assumed — the first lesson starts at the shopping list.
Photo copiers
You can copy a reference but cannot invent a sky from nothing.
Flat-sky painters
Your clouds keep going flat, grey or muddy and you cannot see why.

lessons.title: Welcome & materials for skies
lessons.subtitle: The small kit — one round brush, one flat, three tubes and decent paper.

lessons.title: Seeing clouds as simple shapes
lessons.subtitle: Map cumulus volumes with overlapping circles, the way you would construct a figure.

lessons.title: Pencil sketching & hatching volume
lessons.subtitle: Hatching sets the weight and form before any paint arrives.

lessons.title: Mapping a cloudscape
lessons.subtitle: Thumbnails first — horizon low, masses balanced, nothing wasted.

lessons.title: Reading light, grey and dark
lessons.subtitle: Sort a reference photo into just three value families.

lessons.title: Where the sun hits
lessons.subtitle: Place the lit face of one cloud, then make every other cloud agree.

lessons.title: Shadow shapes that stay soft
lessons.subtitle: Warm-grey undersides that glow instead of going muddy.

lessons.title: A three-value cloud study
lessons.subtitle: One cumulus, three values, twenty minutes — flat shapes become an object.

lessons.title: Cumulus — bold & puffy
lessons.subtitle: Big shapes first, crisp sunlit tops, soft shadowed bellies.

lessons.title: Stratus — streaks on the horizon
lessons.subtitle: One well-loaded stroke, pulled sideways, does most of the work.

lessons.title: Wispy cirrus edges
lessons.subtitle: Barely-there wisps with a thirsty brush and a light hand.

lessons.title: Mixing cloud types in one sky
lessons.subtitle: Layer cumulus over stratus without the sky turning busy.

clouds-intermediate.title: Painting Clouds — Intermediate
clouds-intermediate.blurb: The techniques that separate a study from a painting. Wet-on-wet edges, gradient washes, guarded whites — then three full scenes where all of it runs at once.
learn: Time a wet-on-wet edge by the shine on the paper, not by fiddling
Lay a smooth gradient wash that a cloud can actually sit on
Plan and guard your whites instead of rescuing them later
Take a sky from reference to finished scene on your own
who: Beginner graduates
You have finished the Beginner course and want control, not luck.
Comfortable with washes
You can lay a wash but the edges and whites still get away from you.
Scene painters
Your subject is fine but the sky behind it lets the painting down.

lessons.title: Wet-on-wet cloud edges
lessons.subtitle: Soft, seamless transitions — control the chaos with timing, not fiddling.

lessons.title: Gradient washes for skies
lessons.subtitle: Load a bead, tilt the board, walk away.

lessons.title: Negative painting & hard edges
lessons.subtitle: The brightest highlight is paper you never touched.

lessons.title: Lifting & softening
lessons.subtitle: The rescue kit — a damp brush, clean tissue, and knowing when to stop.

lessons.title: Storm clouds over the ocean
lessons.subtitle: First full scene: everything from the values module, at full volume.

lessons.title: Evening silhouettes & power lines
lessons.subtitle: A peaceful dusk silhouette — quiet, graphic, easier than it looks.

lessons.title: Composing a full cloudscape
lessons.subtitle: Reference, thumbnails, value plan, palette — and I paint alongside you.

little-house.title: Little House in Watercolour
little-house.blurb: A single, self-contained study: one small house, start to finish, in one sitting.
learn: Block in a simple building without a ruler
Keep a roof, a wall and a shadow reading as three different values
Finish a small painting in one sitting
who: Short-project painters
You want something complete in one sitting.
Between courses
A small, self-contained study to keep the brush moving.

lessons.title: Painting a little house
lessons.subtitle: A full watercolour study from pencil sketch to final wash.

urban-sketch.title: Urban Sketching in Watercolour
urban-sketch.blurb: Line and wash on location — buildings, street and figures, painted quickly and loosely.
learn: Draw a street scene fast, in ink, without measuring
Drop colour over line without losing the drawing
Suggest figures and cars with three strokes each
who: Sketchbook painters
You draw on the move and want colour without slowing down.
Outdoor painters
You want to paint on location without carrying a studio.

lessons.title: Urban sketching in watercolour
lessons.subtitle: Line and wash on location: buildings, street and figures.

mountain.title: Mountains in watercolour
mountain.desc: A full mountain study, wet-on-wet from the sky down — the same value thinking as the cloud course, applied to rock.

pink-floral.title: Loose pink florals
pink-floral.desc: Petals in three strokes. A short, forgiving demo for anyone nervous about painting flowers.

watercolor-airport.title: Watercolour airport sketch
watercolor-airport.desc: An on-location sketch from an airport window — line and wash, thirty minutes, nothing precious.
